The Ultimate Tax Deed Investing Guide in Chatham County!

If you’re looking for a new way to build wealth, consider tax deed investing in Chatham County, Georgia. Chatham County offers lucrative opportunities for savvy investors with its thriving job market, lower taxes, and ongoing revitalization efforts.

What Makes Chatham County a Great Place to Invest?

  • Thriving Job Market: Chatham County boasts numerous career opportunities, enhancing financial stability for residents.
  • Lower Taxes: Enjoy higher returns on your investments due to the county’s lower tax rates.
  • Comprehensive Revitalization Plan: The county’s ambitious plans ensure property values are likely to appreciate over time.
  • Natural Beauty: Chatham County is an outdoor enthusiast’s paradise, featuring 24 miles of trails and 20 parks.

Understanding Tax Deed Sales

Tax deed sales in Chatham County provide a way to acquire properties below market value or secure a substantial return on investment. Here’s how it works:

  • Sale Schedule: Tax sales are held on the first Tuesday of each scheduled month at 10:00 AM at the Chatham County Courthouse.
  • Redemption Period: Property owners have one year to redeem their property by paying the sale amount, subsequent taxes, and a premium.
  • Foreclosure Process: If the property is not redeemed within 12 months, the purchaser can start foreclosure to gain full ownership.

Steps to Start Tax Deed Investing

Research Local Laws: Understanding the legal framework is crucial. Key regulations to consider include O.C.G.A. § 9-13-167, which emphasizes “buyer beware.”

Visit the Tax Commissioner’s Website: The County Tax Commissioner’s website provides essential information, including the tax sale list and auction dates. Visit Chatham County Tax Sale List for details.

Check the Auction Site: The County Courthouse, at 133 Montgomery Street in Savannah, Georgia, hosts the auctions.

Contact the County Office: For additional inquiries, reach out to the Tax Commissioner’s Office at (912) 652-7100 or email tax@chathamcounty.org.

Important Details and Links in Chatham County Tax Deed

Pro Tips

  • Do Your Homework: Investigate properties thoroughly before purchasing.
  • Understand the Risks: Remember, tax deed sales operate under “buyer beware.”
  • Prepare Financially: Ensure you have the required funds ready by the day of the sale.

FAQs for Chatham County Tax Deeds

Q: What happens if I purchase a property at a tax sale?

A: You hold a defeasible title and must wait 12 months before starting the foreclosure process if the property is not redeemed.

Q: How can I find out about upcoming tax sales?

A: Visit the Chatham County Tax Commissioner’s website and check the Tax Sale List.

Q: What are the payment requirements on the day of the sale?

A: Payment must be made by 2:00 PM in the form of a cashier’s check, money order, or cash.
